wy_home_alone.blurb: Home Alone is a cluster of walls and alcoves tucked low in Ten Sleep Canyon, just off the highway, so the walk-in is only a couple of minutes. Because the faces point south, east and north, you can chase warmth or escape heat by switching walls. The 19 routes are mostly bolted, with two trad lines, and range from easy 5.5 terrain up to 5.13, with the bulk of the climbing between 5.10 and 5.11. One wall here is a taller, lower-angle face that reads from the trees as you hike in, which makes it a handy spot for the moderate end of the range.

wy_sector_shinto.blurb: Sector Shinto is a quiet sport wall high in Ten Sleep Canyon, reached by a forest trail from the French Cattle Ranch side. All 19 routes are bolted, mostly steep and technical with crimpy, footwork-heavy moves. Grades run from 5.8 up to the low 5.12s, and the great majority fall between 5.10 and 5.12, so it suits climbers who already lead solid 5.10 or harder. Tall trees throw shade over the face through the middle of the day, which helps in warm weather but can leave some holds damp. Expect solitude compared with the busier canyon crags.
wy_sector_shinto.approach: A forest trail of roughly 20 to 30 minutes leads here from the French Cattle Ranch side.

wy_wine_and_roses.blurb: Wine and Roses sits on the north rim of Fremont Canyon, up river from the bridge area, where the walls drop deeper to the North Platte. Nearly all of the 19 routes are trad, with a single sport line, and the star attraction is a 90-foot arching crack that moves from fingers to hands above the water. Grades start at 5.9 and run to the upper end of the scale, with most routes between 5.9 and 5.12 and a pair of much harder lines. Climbs are set up with anchors on the rim, so bring a standard trad rack and a rope long enough for the drop.

wy_spaghetti_aka_third_lost_wall.blurb: Spaghetti, also called Third Lost Wall, is a small formation at Vedauwoo near Laramie, topped with boulders. Of its 18 climbs, eleven are bouldering problems and seven are short trad lines. The problems here are crack-flavoured: overhung hand cracks, an offwidth roof, fist and flared-hands problems. Boulder grades start at the easy end of the V scale, with several in the V0 to V2 range and a few much harder problems up high, while the roped lines sit mostly between 5.8 and 5.11. Bring a pad and plenty of jams, since this is Vedauwoo crack climbing at its most direct.

wy_the_pomeroy_wall.blurb: The Pomeroy Wall, also known as the Hogs Back, stands in the upper Pomeroy basin of the southern Wyoming Range, within reach of Kemmerer. It offers 18 climbs, mostly trad with three sport lines and one top-rope, and the character is friendly slab climbing, some of it with roofs higher up. Grades are modest: most routes fall between 5.6 and 5.8, with a lone line near 5.10. A long rope, a set of draws and a rack are all worth bringing, and the drive in ends right at the base of the wall.

wy_d_hot_tamale_wall.blurb: Hot Tamale Wall is a section of the Main Wall at Wild Iris, easy to spot by its huge undercut base. All 18 routes are bolted, and the draw is a strong cluster of hard pocketed lines: six sit in the 5.12 range, with a few more at 5.11 and a 5.13 on top. A handful of easier routes, starting around 5.7, give moderate climbers something to do. The dolomite is bulging and pocketed, and the Main Wall as a whole faces south, so it catches sun for most of the day. Reach it by any trail to the Main Wall, then walk to the west end.
wy_d_hot_tamale_wall.approach: Follow any of the trails up to the Main Wall and walk to its western end.

wy_grand_wall.blurb: Grand Wall is a pleasant crag at the end of the road in Teton Canyon. It holds 18 climbs, split between bolted routes and trad lines, plus a single boulder problem. The wall faces mostly south, but it stays shaded until about midday and trees cover the belay spots later, so it is workable in summer. Climbing is technical, on slick feet, and the grades span a wide range: 5.6 and 5.7 starters, a solid block of 5.9 to 5.11, and a few lines at 5.12 and 5.13. A short climbers' trail off the canyon path gets you to the base.
wy_grand_wall.approach: From the lot, join the main canyon trail briefly, then take the climbers' trail that forks left; it takes roughly five minutes to reach the base.
